Summarize a joint-manifold Condor workflow run

summarize_joint_estimation.Rd

Reads the output directory of condor_joint_manifold_workflow.py (package inst/condor/) and produces a self-contained Markdown report covering the diagnostics this project has repeatedly needed by hand for each new dataset run through that workflow: whether the per-participant position and alpha estimates actually converged (estimated independently of each other – geometry position and choice-model shape are not tied to a single shared curve; see condor_joint_manifold_update.R's own documentation for why), and – when the original triplet data is supplied – whether the kernel-smoothed production estimate beats each participant's own individual embedding on held-out validation trials, with the embedding-pooling and alpha-shrinkage contributions to that advantage reported separately (not just their combined effect, which conflates the two – see Why the decomposition, not just one comparison below).

Usage

summarize_joint_estimation(
  output_dir,
  triplet_data = NULL,
  run_loo_check = TRUE,
  fit_sample_alg = "random",
  val_trialtype = "validation",
  oscillation_window = 5,
  oscillation_threshold = 0.1,
  item_colors = NULL,
  n_geometry_panels = 6,
  output_md = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

output_dir

Path to a condor_joint_manifold_workflow.py output directory (must contain run_manifest.txt, setup/worker_ids.txt, and setup/item_order.txt – written by that workflow's resume-support code).

triplet_data

NULL (default), or a combined triplet data frame in this package's standard format (Center/Left/ Right/Answer/sampleAlg/worker_id columns – the same shape get.combined produces, or one element of icon_triplets/color_triplets row-bound together). When supplied, this is the original raw triplet data (including validation trials), not anything already inside output_dir – validation trials are deliberately never passed to the Condor workflow itself (see assign_sample_sets()'s "holdout" mode), so there is no way to recover them from output_dir alone. If NULL, the held-out comparison and leave-one-out check are skipped and the report says so.

run_loo_check

Logical. When triplet_data is supplied, also run loo_trajectory_accuracy (fully out-of-sample, no alpha component, not expensive – refits a simple kernel-smoothed trajectory once per participant using each participant's original embedding, not the full joint alternating procedure). Default TRUE.

fit_sample_alg, val_trialtype

Which sampleAlg/trial type counts as fitting vs. held-out data, passed to the internal trial-list builder and to loo_trajectory_accuracy's trialtype. Defaults "random" and "validation", matching this project's standard convention.

oscillation_window, oscillation_threshold

A participant is flagged as possibly not converged if their position's range (or, separately, their log-alpha's range – position and alpha are estimated independently now, so each gets its own convergence check) over the last oscillation_window outer iterations exceeds oscillation_threshold times the full sample's final-iteration range on that same scale. Defaults 5 and 0.1 – tuned against a real non-convergent position case (oscillation amplitude ~0.35 against a full range of ~1.4, comfortably above this threshold) and several genuinely converged boundary cases (recent-iteration range under 0.01). Not a universal constant; adjust if a dataset's own position or alpha scale makes the default too strict or too lax.

item_colors

Character vector, same length and order as setup/item_order.txt, or NULL (default): colors for the embedding-geometry grid. With no dataset-specific semantics available in general, the default colors items by their position in item_order.txt via rainbow; pass a semantically meaningful vector (e.g. an hsv() scheme keyed to known item properties) for a more informative plot.

n_geometry_panels

Integer, number of evenly-spaced query points across the recovered position range to show in the embedding-geometry grid. Default 6. Only plotted when d (read from run_manifest.txt) is 2 or 3; skipped (with a note in the report) otherwise.

output_md

Path to write the Markdown report to. Default file.path(output_dir, "summary.md"). Figures are written as PNG files to a sibling <name>_files/ directory and referenced with relative paths, so the report is self-contained if copied as a unit.

verbose

Logical, print progress. Default TRUE.

Value

Invisibly, a list with the parsed run (run), the convergence diagnostics (position_flags, alpha_flags), and – when triplet_data was supplied – the comparison table (decomposition) and the leave-one-out result (loo, or NULL if run_loo_check = FALSE). Also writes output_md and its figures as a side effect.

Why the decomposition, not just one comparison

The production comparison (pooled estimate vs. each participant's own embedding) differs from the baseline in two ways at once: a pooled vs. individual embedding, and a shrinkage-regularized vs. fixed (alpha = 1) choice-model noise parameter. A win on that comparison alone does not say which component is responsible – alpha-shrinkage alone could help even if the embedding geometry carries no real cross-participant structure at all, simply by partially pooling a single scalar noise parameter toward a population mean. This function reports all four combinations (own/pooled embedding x alpha=1/shrunk) so that conclusion doesn't have to be taken on faith; see the triplet_choice_and_loss.Rmd analysis (outside this package, in the lab's own research documentation) this was first worked out in for a worked example on real data, where embedding-pooling alone (holding alpha fixed) already recovered most of the combined effect – and where that same analysis went on to test whether alpha's regularization needed to be tied to geometric position at all (an earlier design this workflow used) and found no advantage to doing so, which is why alpha is decoupled from position in the current design.

There is a second, independent confound even within "embedding-pooling alone": the kernel-smoothed pooled estimate differs from a participant's own embedding both by averaging in other participants and by being evaluated at that participant's own recovered position – itself a free parameter fit to that participant's own training data. A plain, position-independent grand mean (the same embedding for every participant) isolates the first effect without the second. Comparing it to the position-weighted pooled estimate answers whether a participant's own position is doing anything beyond ordinary variance-reduction from averaging – on one real dataset analyzed this way, the two were statistically indistinguishable (no evidence of real position-dependent structure, just noise reduction), while on another they were not (the position-weighted estimate did reliably better, consistent with a real individual-differences axis).
